- ooc-sort-dev: Use when developing, building, testing, or iterating on the disk-backed (out-of-core) sort implementation for cudf-polars in ~/bzaitlen/test-data/ooc-sort/. Covers installing into the rapidsmpf container env, running streaming sort tests, and the phase-by-phase implementation workflow.
- build-errors: Use this skill when the build fails, compilation errors occur, or you see undefined references, linker errors, CUDA compilation issues, missing headers, or template instantiation failures. Analyzes errors, suggests fixes, and iteratively rebuilds until success.
- build-sirius-starrocks: Build the Sirius-as-StarRocks-CN stack on a fresh GPU box — UCX, nixl, libsirius, StarRocks FE, and the Rust CN. Use when standing the stack up from scratch, recovering a broken toolchain (g++/ld/nvml shims, CUDA 13, no-root conda deps), applying the StarRocks proto patch, or relocating pixi/cargo/Maven onto local NVMe.
- cn-tuning: Size Sirius StarRocks CN memory and operator budgets for a given GPU box and TPC-H scale factor. Use when choosing GPU_MEM, STAGING, HOST_MEM, hash_partition_bytes, scan_task_batch_size, or when a query OOMs / exhausts the exchange arena / looks like an engine bug that is actually mis-sizing. Covers the derived-flag path vs a full sirius.yaml.
- dataset-manager: Use this skill to generate benchmark datasets (TPC-H, TPC-DS, etc.). Trigger when the user needs test data at a specific scale factor for benchmarking or testing. Supports parquet and duckdb output formats.
- log-analyzer: Use this skill to analyze Sirius query execution logs — to find why a query is slow, diagnose validation errors (wrong results), spot excessive downgrading, identify pipeline gaps, or compare two runs of the same query. Trigger whenever the user mentions a Sirius log file, says "look at this log", asks about per-operator time, pipeline gaps, memory pressure, downgrade behavior, validation/correctness mismatches, or wants to compare two query runs. Also use as a hand-off target from race-check (for two-run comparisons), runtime-errors (for "where did the query stall before hang"), and validate (for diffing the bad run against a good run). This is the log-only counterpart to profile-analyzer (nsys) and optimization-advisor (source-level guidance).
- module-context: Automatically identify which dependency library modules are relevant to a task and load their API documentation into context. Use PROACTIVELY before implementing features, fixing bugs, or writing new operators — analyzes the task description and loads cudf, rmm, duckdb, cucascade module docs to improve code quality. Trigger when the user asks to implement, add, fix, or modify GPU operators, pipeline components, memory management, joins, aggregations, sorting, expressions, or data I/O.
- module-discover: Discover and document a dependency library or submodule — analyzes all uses within the codebase, divides the library into logical modules, identifies which modules are used, and generates LLM-consumable API documentation for each module. Use when the user wants to understand a library dependency, map its modules, or generate API reference docs for a submodule.
- optimization-advisor: Use this skill to find exactly which source code to optimize for better GPU performance. Maps nsys profile hotspots to specific Sirius source files and functions, classifies bottlenecks as GPU-bound, CPU-bound, or sync-bound, and recommends actionable code changes. Trigger when the user wants to know what to optimize, where to focus coding effort, or wants source-level optimization guidance. This skill focuses on actionable source code targets — for generating performance reports and measurements, use profile-analyzer instead.
- pr-digest: Generates a "learning" PR-review digest — a markdown file at PR_digests/PR_digest_<N>.md that explains what a GitHub PR does, why, and exactly where in the code, with clickable file/line links and trimmed diffs. Use this whenever the user shares a GitHub PR URL (e.g. github.com/owner/repo/pull/1234) and wants to understand, summarize, review, walk through, or get up to speed on what changed — phrases like "can you review this PR", "what does this PR do", "help me understand this pull request", "summarize the changes in PR
- pre-commit-cleanup: Clean the current Git changes before committing. Use when preparing to commit or when the pre-commit cleanliness hook blocks a commit.
- profile-analyzer: Use this skill to understand why a Sirius query is slow, identify GPU bottlenecks, or detect performance regressions. Generates reports with kernel occupancy, memory bandwidth, operator attribution, and cross-run comparisons. Trigger when the user mentions profiling, nsys, GPU utilization, kernel analysis, performance reports, or wants to compare query timings across runs. This skill focuses on measurement and reporting — for mapping hotspots to source code fixes, use optimization-advisor instead.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- tpch-2host: Bring up Sirius StarRocks CNs across two physical GB200 hosts with nixl over cross-host NVLink, and the matching stock StarRocks (engine B) two-machine baseline. Use when replicating the two-host experiment, setting SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_ARENA=fabric, debugging a 0.4 GB/s cuda_ipc fallback, or running engine B as 1 FE + 1 BE per host.
- tpch-bench: Operate the Sirius-as-StarRocks-CN demo and its TPC-H benchmark on the 4x GB200 box. Use when bringing the multi-GPU (N-CN, one CN per GPU) cluster up or down, running a query or the 22-query sweep, verifying the nixl/NVLink transport, triaging a failing/hanging/slow query, checking results against DuckDB, or reproducing the A-vs-B comparison against stock StarRocks.
- tpch-cn-sweep: Run the 22-query TPC-H sweep against a Sirius StarRocks CN cluster on any box, scale factor, data path, or GPU count. Use when launching bench.sh, sizing GPU_MEM/STAGING, checking results against the DuckDB oracle, or triaging pass/wedge/refused rows. Not the in-process Sirius-vs-DuckDB benchmark skill; not the GB200-hardcoded tpch-bench ops skill.

Trigger when the user says "update docs", "refresh documentation", "sync docs with code changes", or after merging PRs that changed the Super Sirius codebase. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

# SF1000 profiling: planning / cardinality / backpressure — evidence bundle and analysis plan

Build: worktree /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf, branch perf/profile-sf1000 = d24f02c4 + 85658f09 (aggregate gate) +
9a5a4da6 (async sender dispatch) + 45dab3be (Quent probes: scan_split_read, stream hops, staging leases, CN fragment labels).
Data: /scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000 (decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table). Queries: experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql.

## Evidence (scratchpad = /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000)
- survey/explain/qNN.costs.txt, qNN.verbose.txt   FE EXPLAIN COSTS / VERBOSE for all 22 queries (fragments, join distribution, cardinality: 1 everywhere)
- survey/plan-summary.txt                          explain_summary.py over all 22 (joins with build/probe children and broadcast tables)
- cn1/  cn4/  standalone/                           the three arms; each has runs/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc), runs/qNN.rK.out(.err)
- cn1/cluster.log, cn4/cluster.log                  FE + CN logs (fragment run started/finished, declared input stream cardinality, relayed batches, transmitted batches via nixl, OOM reschedule warnings)
- cn1/dump/fragment-*.txt, plan-*.substrait         every fragment the FE sent to the 1-CN and the translator's Substrait plan
- cn1/quent/.cnN/<session>/, cn4/quent/.cnN/<session>/, standalone/quent/<session>/   Quent ndjson (task FSM, data_batch, batch_placement, memory, scan_split_read)
- standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt                   DuckDB/Sirius EXPLAIN of the same SQL (the stats-aware planner's choice)
- <arm>-cnlog.json (cnlog_extract.py), <arm>-quent.txt / .json (quent_bp.py), card-compare-<arm>.txt (card_compare.py), results.md (results_table.py)
- ../../oracle/tpch_sf1000/qNN.tsv                  DuckDB CPU oracle answers; compare-*.txt

## Tools (same dir)
explain_summary.py, cnlog_extract.py, card_compare.py, quent_bp.py, results_table.py, ../quent_summary.py (per-operator Computing sums)

## Facts established before the analysis
1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.

## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
A. Planning: per query, FE fragment tree and join distribution vs the DuckDB/Sirius standalone plan; what a stats-aware FE would choose; where the translator/CN could override (e.g. swap build/probe, refuse broadcast above a row threshold, local re-planning of a broadcast join once the actual parked cardinality is known).
B. Cardinality: FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange (card_compare), engine reservation estimate vs peak (quent_bp), the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism and its cost.
C. Backpressure: parked bytes and dwell per fragment, staging lease held/in-transit time and max concurrency vs SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, Reserving/Queued waits, OOM reschedule storms, nixl transmit lease_ms/write_ms, 1-CN vs 4-CN scaling per query, standalone vs CN.
Each per-query analysis is verified adversarially (two skeptics with different lenses); the synthesis ranks findings with the evidence lines and proposes changes with file paths and confidence.

## Facts added after the 1-CN sweep (13:19 UTC)
5. Supported on the CN path at SF1000 (1 CN, 100 GiB pool): q01 q02 q03 q04 q06 q07 q10 q11 q12 q13 q14 q15 q19 q20 q22 pass (15). Fail: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 = OOM at GPU_SCAN after 100 reschedules
   (101 s, 168 s, 232 s, 104 s, 54 s, 114 s to die; 2500-5600 reschedule warnings each, see cn1-cnlog.txt); q16 = translator gap ("multi_distinct_count has a partial state this translator does not model").
6. q15 returned 0 rows in run 1 and 1 row in runs 0 and 2 on 1 CN: streams 18 and 22 (the revenue = max(revenue) join output) carried 0 rows in run 1 while every other stream was identical.
   The build has the canonical float-sum sort gated OFF (SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS unset), so the two independently computed FP64 sums can differ in the last bits. Follow-up arms cn1-canon-q15 / cn1-nocanon-q15 test this.
7. Engine executor pools default to pipeline num_threads: 4 (docs/super-sirius/configuration.md:91-94); Quent "Queued" time per fragment is the wait for one of those slots plus the memory reservation gate.
   1-CN q04: scan fragment 37 tasks, Queued sum 19.9 s vs Computing 4.7 s inside a 1.2 s wall; join fragment requested 253 GB of reservations for a 61 GB summed peak (4x over-estimate).
8. Translator comment (node_translator.rs ~1924-1931) already records that the FE reports cardinality 1 for every FILES() scan and that nothing bounds a join build side; "bounding it belongs to the executor".
9. FE plans with 4 CNs alive are in survey/explain4/ (plan-summary-4cn.txt); diff against plan-summary.txt shows whether node count changes any distribution decision.
10. Plan-node enum decode for the dumps (TPlanNodeType(N)): survey/TPlanNodeType.map.txt (4 HASH_JOIN, 6 AGGREGATION, 8 SORT, 9 EXCHANGE, 17 FILE_SCAN, 28 PROJECT, ...).
11. The engine's DuckDB optimizer runs on every fragment (sirius_ffi.cpp:135, with STATISTICS_PROPAGATION and a few rewrites disabled, :233-240); the declared stream cardinality feeds the TableFunction cardinality callback (stream_bind_catalog.hpp:44-46), so build/probe choice inside a fragment sees exact stream sizes, but FILES() scans inside the same fragment carry DuckDB's parquet estimate. The FE's fragment cut (what is broadcast/shuffled) is fixed before any of this.
12. The FE's plan DEPENDS on the number of alive CNs even with cardinality 1 everywhere: with 4 CNs most joins flip from BROADCAST to PARTITIONED (shuffle) and fragment counts rise (q02 13->16, q08 11->16, q09 9->12; q03 orders join BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q04/q12/q14/q19 BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q15 -> BUCKET_SHUFFLE). survey/plan-summary.txt (1 CN) vs survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt (4 CNs); card-compare-cn4.txt uses the 4-CN plans (q03 exch2 = 3.23B lineitem rows shuffled, q12 exch1 = 1.5B orders rows shuffled).
13. 4-CN staging leases per query (cn4-quent.txt, attributed by time): q07.r1 747 leases / 141.5 GB moved / 92.9 s summed lease-held time inside a 1.79 s query, max 64 concurrent leases per CN; q04.r1 360 leases / 48.8 GB; q01.r1 14 leases / 0.06 GB. Session-wide per CN ~3700 leases, max 94 concurrent (arena = 16 GiB).
14. Standalone (one GPU, 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics) runs the same 15 queries; standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt holds its plans. 1-CN vs standalone warm medians (ms): q01 5073/4882, q02 1246/571, q03 3106/3050, q07 3476/3266, q11 970/336, q15 4685/2627, q20 4171/3023, q22 943/496 (results.md).
15. Pre-digested tables added: reservation-ratio.txt (per run: tasks, summed reservation request vs summed measured peak, ratio, summed Queued and Computing seconds, wall; cn1 q11 54x, q14 15x, q03 14x, q10 6x over-reservation), cn4-transmits.txt (nixl transmits per run: count, GB, elapsed/lease/write ms, write GB/s).
16. Correctness vs the DuckDB oracle (compare-cn1.txt, compare-cn4.txt, compare-standalone.txt; rel tol 1e-6): standalone 15/15 MATCH. CN arms: q02 q04 q06 q12 q13 q14 q20 q22 MATCH; q01 q07 q19 differ by 9.6e-4 and q03 by 1.8e-3 in revenue sums (the known `1 - 0.07` FP64->DECIMAL(16,2) truncation from #1236's lowering, not a multi-CN defect); q10 differs with maxreldiff 12.3 over 48 cells of its 20 rows, most likely the same truncated revenue sums reordering the TOP-20 (verify by comparing the customer sets and the revenue column); q15 differs by 1.1e-3 on its single row and is also flaky in row count (see fact 6); q11 shows EMPTY because the query returns 0 rows at SF1000 on both engines (the bench kit does not scale q11's 0.0001 fraction by 1/SF), so it is not a defect but the compare cannot confirm it.
17. results-ratios.md: 1-CN parity T_sr1/T_standalone is 0.95-1.2 for the scan-heavy queries (q01 q03 q04 q06 q07 q12 q14 q19), 1.2-1.4 for q10 q13 q20, and 1.8-2.9 for the fragment-heavy small ones (q02 2.18, q11 2.88, q15 1.78, q22 1.90); 4-CN speed-up over 1 CN is 1.7-2.35x (efficiency 0.43-0.59) for the scan-heavy queries and 1.08-1.46x for q02 q11 q22.
18. Follow-up arms (may still be running while you work; use them only if their files exist): standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv (standalone Sirius on q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21), cn1-canon-q15/runs/runs.csv (1 CN, SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1, 6 runs of q15) vs cn1-nocanon-q15/runs/runs.csv (gate off).
19. DONE: standalone Sirius (same GPU, same 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics, pipelined execution) runs every query the CN path could not: q05 5191/2786 ms (pass, rows=5), q08 3835/3674 ms (pass, rows=2), q09 6818/5427 ms (pass, rows=175), q17 4386/3786 ms (pass, rows=1), q18 2764/2691 ms (pass, rows=100), q21 6534/6401 ms (pass, rows=100) (cold/warm; standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv, plans in standalone-failed/runs/qNN.explain.txt, Quent in standalone-failed/quent/). The CN path died on the same queries after 54-232 s of OOM reschedules. This is the central planning + backpressure contrast of the campaign.
20. DONE q15 determinism A/B on 1 CN (6 runs each): SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1 -> rows per run ['0', '1', '0', '0', '1', '0'] (ms ['10331', '5161', '5182', '5002', '4876', '4809']); gate off -> rows ['0', '0', '1', '0', '0', '0'] (ms ['10576', '4795', '4847', '4799', '4661', '4788']). Files: cn1-canon-q15/, cn1-nocanon-q15/ (runs, cluster.log, quent, engine-*.log).
21. CORRECTION to fact 6: the A/B in fact 20 REFUTES the simple hypothesis that the SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS gate alone explains q15's empty runs: with the canonical sort ON, 4 of 6 runs still return 0 rows (gate off: 5 of 6). The gate only canonicalizes row order inside the update-phase aggregate; the FE plan computes the revenue CTE twice (two independent two-phase aggregations over FP64-lowered decimals) and then joins on `total_revenue = max(total_revenue)`. Batch arrival order into the merge phase (and therefore FP64 summation order) still varies run to run, so the two sums can differ in the last bits and the equality join yields nothing. Standalone Sirius keeps DECIMAL and returns the row every time. Treat this as a correctness finding about equality joins on FP64-lowered aggregates on the CN path; verify from cn1-canon-q15/ and cn1-nocanon-q15/ logs (declared cardinalities of streams 18/22 per run) and the translator's decimal->FP64 lowering (#1236, cast_to_fp64 in expr_translator.rs).
22. compare-standalone-failed.txt: standalone results for q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 vs the DuckDB oracle: q05=MATCH q08=MATCH q09=MATCH q17=MATCH q18=MATCH q21=MATCH

379 REPORT.md
# SF1000 TPC-H on StarRocks-on-Sirius: planning, cardinality, backpressure

Audience: Sirius engineers. Evidence root: `scratchpad/perf/sf1000` (paths below are relative to it unless they start with `src/`, `experimental/`, `duckdb/`, `cucascade/`, which are relative to the source worktree `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf`). FE = `experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks`.

Every number below is either **measured** (copied from a named evidence file) or marked **inference**. Line numbers for the load-bearing source citations (StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676, gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:348/409, streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112, node_translator.rs:1743-1762, compute_node_service.rs:468, engine.rs:278-280, exchange_staging_arena.cpp:248, HashJoinCostModel.java:115-127) were re-checked against the worktree at `45dab3be` while writing this report.

---

## 1. Setup

### Build and data

| item | value |
|---|---|
| worktree | `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf`, branch `perf/profile-sf1000` = `d24f02c4` + `85658f09` (aggregate gate) + `9a5a4da6` (async sender dispatch) + `45dab3be` (Quent probes: scan reads, stream hops, staging leases, CN fragment labels) |
| data | `/scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000`, decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table; lineitem 5,999,989,709 rows in 60 files (166 GiB on GPFS), orders 1.5e9, partsupp 8e8, customer 1.5e8, part 2e8, supplier 1e7 (parquet footers, agent-notes/planning-contrast.md) |
| storage | `/scratch` is GPFS; the uring datasource opens files `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECT` (`src/io/uring/uring_reactor.cpp:528`, `src/include/io/uring/config.hpp:27-28`), so warm runs re-read from GPFS, not the page cache |
| queries | `experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql`; every file declares all 8 tables as `WITH ... FILES()` CTEs |
| oracle | DuckDB CPU answers in `../../oracle/tpch_sf1000/qNN.tsv`, compared at rel tol 1e-6 |

### Arms

| arm | what ran | configuration |
|---|---|---|
| `cn1` | StarRocks FE + 1 Sirius CN, all 22 queries | `GPU_MEM=100GiB HOST_MEM=160GiB STAGING=16GiB SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES=16GiB SIRIUS_QUERY_WATCHDOG_SECS=300 SIRIUS_CN_ENABLE_QUENT=1 SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1` (capture-cn.sh:11-12); fragment dumps on (`SIRIUS_CN_DUMP_FRAGMENTS`); executor pipeline pool 4 threads (default, docs/super-sirius/configuration.md:91-94) |
| `cn4` | FE + 4 CNs (one per GPU), the 15 queries that passed on `cn1` | same |
| `standalone` | DuckDB + Sirius extension in-process on GPU 0, same 15 queries | `sirius-standalone-quent.yaml`: usage_limit 100 GiB, host 160 GiB; DuckDB planner with parquet statistics; measured in-process by `standalone_run_labeled.py` |
| `standalone-failed` | same, the 6 queries that failed on `cn1` | `sirius-standalone-quent-failed.yaml` (same limits) |
| `cn1-canon-q15` / `cn1-nocanon-q15` | 1 CN, 6 runs of q15 with `SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1` / unset | as `cn1` |

Each query ran once cold then twice warm; `results.md` reports the warm median (n=2). `run-queries.sh:19` stops a query after a failing cold run, so failed queries have one run. CN client timing is a `mysql` process per run (`run-queries.sh`), which adds 17-57 ms of process spawn and a failing `select @@version_comment limit 1` handshake statement per run (measured: FE AuditLog Time vs client wall, cn1 q11.r1 951 vs 969 ms, cn4 q11.r1 606 vs 663 ms). Standalone timing is in-process (9-22 ms outside the engine span).

FE-side plans for all 22 queries were captured with 1 CN alive (`survey/explain/qNN.costs.txt`, `survey/plan-summary.txt`) and with 4 CNs alive (`survey/explain4/`, `survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt`). During the 1-CN survey the FE still had four CNs registered with three dead (survey/cluster.log ids 10001, 11001, 12002, 12003), which matters for one cost-model term (section 3A, finding P3).

### How "supported" was decided

A query is "supported on the CN path at SF1000" if the cold run on `cn1` returned rows without error. The 4-CN arm ran only those. Nothing was excluded a priori.

| outcome | queries | reason (measured) |
|---|---|---|
| pass on 1 CN (15) | q01 q02 q03 q04 q06 q07 q10 q11 q12 q13 q14 q15 q19 q20 q22 | `cn1/runs/runs.csv` |
| fail, GPU OOM (6) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 | `cn1/runs/qNN.r0.err`: `GPU pipeline task exceeded maximum retry limit (100) ... OOM at operator GPU_SCAN (index 0)`; 101,460 / 168,285 / 232,533 / 103,894 / 54,202 / 114,485 ms to die; 2500 / 3600 / 5600 / 2100 / 2300 / 1800 reschedule warnings (cn1-cnlog.txt lines 14, 21, 22, 42, 43, 50) |
| fail, translator gap (1) | q16 | `cn1/runs/q16.r0.err`: `malformed plan: two-phase aggregation supports only sum/count/min/max/avg; "multi_distinct_count" has a partial state this translator does not model (SET new_planner_agg_stage = 1)`; 356 ms |

Standalone Sirius on the same GPU and the same 100 GiB pool ran all six OOM queries (results-failed.md): q05 5191/2786 ms, q08 3835/3674, q09 6818/5427, q17 4386/3786, q18 2764/2691, q21 6534/6401 (cold/warm), all matching the oracle (compare-standalone-failed.txt). That contrast is the central fact of the campaign.

### Correctness vs the oracle

| query | cn1 | cn4 | standalone | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| q02 q04 q06 q12 q13 q14 q20 q22 | MATCH | MATCH | MATCH | q14 maxreldiff 1.7e-7, q22 1.5e-15 |
| q01 q07 q19 | VALUES-DIFFER 9.6e-4 | same | MATCH | the known `1 - 0.07` FP64 -> DECIMAL(16,2) truncation from the translator's decimal lowering (#1236, `expr_translator.rs:808-836 cast_to_fp64`); identical on cn1 and cn4, so not a multi-CN defect |
| q03 | VALUES-DIFFER 1.8e-3 | same | MATCH | same cause |
| q10 | VALUES-DIFFER maxreldiff 12.3, 48 cells over 20 rows | same | MATCH | most likely the same truncated revenue sums reordering the TOP-20 (inference; the customer sets were not compared) |
| q15 | VALUES-DIFFER 1.1e-3, and 0 rows in some runs | same | MATCH | see below |
| q11 | EMPTY | EMPTY | MATCH rows=0 | the bench kit does not scale q11's 0.0001 fraction by 1/SF, so the query returns 0 rows on both engines at SF1000; not a defect, but the compare cannot confirm it |
| q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 | NO-ORACLE (failed) | not run | MATCH (standalone-failed) | |

**q15 returns 0 rows in roughly half of the CN runs** (measured, `runs.csv` rows column): cn1 1,0,1; cn4 1,0,0; cn1-canon-q15 0,1,0,0,1,0; cn1-nocanon-q15 0,0,1,0,0,0; standalone 1,1,1 (15 of 15). In every 0-row run, streams 18 and 22 (the `total_revenue = max(total_revenue)` join output) declared 0 rows while every other stream was identical (cn1-cnlog.txt lines 38-40: `s18=1, s22=1` in r0/r2, `s18=0, s22=0` in r1). Mechanism (measured plan + source): the FE inlines the `revenue` CTE twice (survey/explain/q15.costs.txt lines 207 and 241 are two lineitem FileScanNodes), the translator lowers the DECIMAL sum to FP64 (`expr_translator.rs:808-836`, `partial_state.rs:1-30`), and the CN compares two independently computed FP64 sums for bit equality. The `SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS` gate was measurably active in the canon arm (HASH_GROUP_BY(2) 0.50-0.62 s vs 0.075-0.105 s, agent-notes/mfs-canon-quent.txt vs mfs-nocanon-quent.txt) and did not fix it (2/6 vs 1/6 correct). Remaining nondeterminism is inferred to be batch composition (atomic chunk cursor `src/scan_manager/sirius_scan_manager.cpp:235-240`, coalescer packing row groups "in any order" `duckdb_native_batch_coalescer.hpp:31-40`). Treat as a correctness bug of equality joins on FP64-lowered aggregates on the CN path; fixes are in section 4 (item 9).

---

## 2. Results

Warm medians (n=2) in ms, from `results.md` and `results-ratios.md`. `-` = not run.

| query | standalone | 1 CN | 4 CN | 1 CN / standalone | 1 CN / 4 CN | efficiency (speed-up / 4) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

Cold runs (results.md): cn1 q01 9359, q22 4110 (the q22 cold run followed q21's failure and ran with a 36.6 GB leak, see finding B4); cn4 q02 2158, q04 2155.

Three groups fall out of this table:

- Scan-heavy queries (q01 q03 q04 q06 q07 q12 q14 q19): 1 CN is at parity with standalone (0.95-1.2x) and 4 CNs give 1.7-2.35x (efficiency 0.43-0.59).
- Fragment-heavy small queries (q02 q11 q22, and q15): 1 CN is 1.8-2.9x slower than standalone and 4 CNs barely help (1.08-1.46x), except q15 (2.30x, because its two full lineitem scans do split).
- Six queries that only standalone can run at this scale.

Run-to-run consistency: cn1 and standalone warm pairs are within 3-5%; cn4 q02 has a 21% spread (1264 vs 1044 ms). The six failures ran once each on both cn1 and standalone-failed.

---

## 3. Findings by dimension

Notation: **P** planning, **C** cardinality, **B** backpressure. Confirmed findings first in each dimension (both a data skeptic and a source skeptic failed to refute them; their corrections are folded in), then disputed findings with the objection stated, then lower-ranked findings that were not adversarially verified (marked as such).

### 3A. Planning

#### P1 (confirmed). The six 1-CN failures are one FE plan shape: an unfiltered lineitem leaf feeding a hash-partitioned exchange, whose whole output must be parked on the GPU

**Measured.** In all six plans the failing fragment is a bare lineitem `FileScanNode` under a `HASH_PARTITIONED` `TDataStreamSink` with one destination (survey/plan-summary.txt lines 10, 16, 18, 34, 36, 42; dumps cn1/dump/fragment-0141 (q05, node 8), 0208 (q08), 0220 (q09), 0427 (q17, node 0), 0437 (q18, node 9), 0504 (q21, node 12), each `output_partition TPartitionType(2)` = HASH_PARTITIONED per `Partitions.thrift:41-49`). The FE join labels differ (q05/q08/q09/q17 PARTITIONED, q18 `11:INNER JOIN (BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S))`, q21 `14:LEFT SEMI JOIN (BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S))`), the sink type does not. Lineitem is the build-side exchange in five plans and the probe-side exchange in q17. Every one of the six failing fragments was started as `role=sender inputs=0 outputs=1` (cn1/cluster.log lines 4200, 7854, 9840, 16770, 18095, 20282).

Because nothing streams across a fragment boundary (finding B1), the sender must park its entire projection. Size of that projection (standalone `GPU_SCAN in=` of the same scan, agent-notes/standalone-failed-quent.txt) versus what fit before the pool filled (cn1-quent.txt `STREAMING_SINK in=`, engine-cn0.log `[gpu_pool] QueryBegin/QueryEnd allocated=`):

| query | lineitem projection (GB) | pool before the sender started (GB) | parked by the sender at death (GB) | pool at death (GB) | stuck tasks x 100 retries |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| q05 | 171.00 | 0.00 | 104.30 | 104.30 | 25 |
| q08 | 195.75 | 4.70 (q05 leftovers) | 99.54 | 104.24 | 36 |
| q09 | 244.50 | 8.83 (q08 leftovers) | 96.42 | 105.24 | 56 |
| q17 | 122.25 | 38.16 (q09 + q16 leftovers) | 66.26 | 104.42 | 21 |
| q18 | 97.50 | 68.69 (own senders: customer 3.94 + agg 24.0 + orders 36.75, plus 4.0 q17 leftover) | 35.87 | 104.56 | 23 |
| q21 | 73.50 (the 28-task l2 leaf) | 77.76 (own filtered l1/l3 sender) | 25.37 | 103.14 | 18 |

Pool cap = 107,374,182,400 bytes (100 GiB); every one of the 17,917 OOM lines in cn1/engine-cn0.log reads `global usage 107374182400 bytes`. `begin + parked = end` holds within 0.01 GB in every row.

Correction to the original claim: "the sender cannot fit its own output" is true for q05/q08/q09/q17 (projection > 107 GB alone) but not for q18 (97.5 GB) or q21 (73.5 GB), which died because the query's other exchange inputs were parked at the same time. The accurate statement is: the sum of concurrently parked exchange inputs of one query (plus leftovers of earlier failed queries, finding B4) exceeds the pool, and nothing can be spilled (finding B2). Per-row widths in the engine are 12-41 B (decimals arrive as 8-byte values), so the analyst's "168-456 GB" range with decimal128 widths overstates three of the six.

**Measured, standalone contrast.** The same SQL on the same GPU and pool passes because DuckDB's stats-aware plan streams lineitem as the probe of a hash join built on the small filtered dimension chain: standalone-failed/runs/q05.explain.txt:50-61 has `READ_PARQUET lineitem ~6,110,827,680 rows` as the probe child with a ~61.6M-row build; q18.explain.txt:37-56 likewise; q17/q21 use DELIM joins. standalone-failed-quent q17 `HASH_JOIN(18) n=46 in=120.54 GB` shows lineitem probing in 46 batches, never materialised. Standalone still materialises lineitem-derived aggregate state (q18 PARTITION(5) 36.19 GB), just not the raw projection.

**Root cause.** `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (FE `sql/optimizer/statistics/StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676`): `// cause we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now` `builder.setOutputRowCount(1)`, every column `ColumnStatistic.unknown()`. card-compare-cn1.txt shows FE estimate 1 for every exchange of the six queries against actuals of 150,000,000 / 227,571,151 (q05 s1/s4) and 730,806,711 (q21 s6). With every side at 1 row the CBO's fragment cut is arithmetic on column widths and node count (finding P3).

**Not measured.** Whether the six pass on 4 CNs. cn4/runs/runs.csv has no rows for them. A hash-partitioned exchange splits parked bytes across CNs (cn4 q03.r1: the 3.23B-row lineitem shuffle parked 19.60/19.67/19.71/19.86 GB per CN), so the per-CN lineitem share would be ~31-61 GB and the expected outcome is pass (inference). The 4-CN plans are also not identical: q21's `10:RIGHT ANTI JOIN` becomes `BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S)` with a local build (plan-summary-4cn.txt line 42).

**Proposed changes.**

1. FE: real FILES() cardinalities (finding C1, section 4 item 3). Caveat from the source skeptic (inference, medium confidence): with real statistics the small side of lineitem's join is orders-derived (q18 ~308M rows, q05 227M rows, tens of GB), `CostModel.java:428` multiplies a broadcast whose build exceeds `exec_mem_limit` (2 GiB, `SessionVariable.java:1305`) by `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY` = 1000, and the shuffle network cost is 0 on a single node (`CostModel.java:437-440`). Real row counts alone may therefore still put lineitem across an exchange on 1 CN; this needs an `EXPLAIN COSTS` with statistics, which was not run.
2. CN, 1-CN only: fuse a leaf scan fragment into its single-destination receiver before translation, at the `TPlan` level (replace the receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE` with the sender's node list; `ExchangeNode.java:183/360` guarantee the row layout matches). On 1 CN every exchange is local, so the fused plan is the standalone plan that passes all six. Substantial work; medium confidence. Caveat: for q21 the fused lineitem would sit on the build side of a `LEFT SEMI` that the translator cannot flip (no `RIGHT_SEMI`, finding P5), so q21 needs P5 as well.
3. Engine: fail fast (finding B3) so a wrong plan costs ~3 s instead of 54-232 s.

Confidence: high on the diagnosis; medium on which fix path is accepted.

#### P2 (confirmed). q02: the FE decorrelates the min-subquery into a full 800M-row partsupp chain and shuffles a 1-row region; its runtime filters are dropped by the CN

**Measured, 1 CN.** card-compare-cn1.txt lines 4-15: exch 3 BROADCAST 800,000,000 rows (partsupp as the build of join 4); exch 28 SHUFFLE 800,000,000 by `n_regionkey` into join 31 PARTITIONED against exch 30 = 1 row (region EUROPE); exch 34/36 = 118,065,576-row min table. survey/explain/q02.costs.txt:305-327 (join 31), 519-535 (join 4), 73-97 (join 37 `build runtime filters filter_id=7 build_expr=ps_partkey remote=true`).

The engine rescues the build side inside F00: cn1-quent.txt:118-122 fragment 56c `DYNAMIC_FILTER(4) n=5 in=13.10GB` -> 0.05 GB, `HASH_JOIN(7)` input 0.07 GB (DuckDB inside the fragment built on the filtered part and join-filtered the parked partsupp stream). The 13.1 GB partsupp stream was still scanned and parked in full (fragment 56d GPU_SCAN 0.788 s). The cost that is not rescued is the subquery chain: fragment 566 (F11, partsupp x supplier x nation) `GPU_SCAN(6) 0.779 + HASH_JOIN(10) 0.289 + HASH_JOIN(14) 0.399 s`, wall 438 ms of a 1.063 s span (41%), plus F19 `HASH_JOIN(7) 0.243 s` over 13.0 GB and the min aggregation. Standalone (standalone-quent.txt:24-29) spends 1.826 s Computing of which 1.769 s is GPU_SCAN (it also scans partsupp twice) and 0.057 s everything else; its `LEFT_DELIM_JOIN` (standalone/runs/q02.explain.txt:52, 142-157) joins the subquery's partsupp with `DELIM_SCAN` (the outer's distinct p_partkeys) before the min aggregation. cn1 Computing 2.9 s vs standalone 1.8 s (reservation-ratio.txt lines 4, 34): the ~1.0 s excess is joins and aggregates over 800M rows.

Runtime filters are dropped, measured: the FE attached filter 6 (`r_regionkey` -> F14 nation scan) and shipped `TRuntimeFilterDescription` entries with `has_remote_targets: true` (cn1/dump/fragment-0025.txt:1074-1275), yet exch 25 delivered all 25 nations (card-compare-cn1.txt, q02 exch 25 row), so exch 28 carried 800M rows instead of ~160M. `grep -rn runtime_filter` over `crates/starrocks-plan-translator/src` and `experimental/starrocks/src` finds only a test fixture (wire_type_parity.rs:607).

**Measured, 4 CN.** The plan changes (13 -> 16 fragments): exch 4, 21, 26, 31 = 800,000,000 rows each (card-compare-cn4.txt lines 4-18; two are raw partsupp scans, two are re-shuffles of the joined 800M-row intermediate on `s_nationkey` and `n_regionkey`), exch 39 BROADCAST = 118,065,576 rows delivered to 4 CNs (card_compare sums receivers, hence "472M"). 135 nixl transmits, 43.6-45.7 GB per run (cn4-transmits.txt). The `n_regionkey` shuffle (5 distinct values) is skewed: cn4-cnlog.json q02.r0 stream 31 per receiver = 479,981,680 / 160,046,880 / 159,971,440 / 0 rows. Total Computing went from 2.9 s to 4.6 s over 4 CNs = 1.15 s per CN, but the span did not move (1.063 -> 1.077 s), Queued = 0: q02 on 4 CNs is wait-dominated.

Two further q02 facts: ~200 ms of the 1-CN vs standalone gap is outside the engine span (finding P4), and on 4 CNs one of the two partsupp scan fragments (c472-c475) ran at 0.21 s/GB while the other (c464-c467) ran at 0.05 s/GB in the same run; that one fragment is 348 ms = 32% of the span and tracks the run-to-run spread (MFS-5, unverified, cause unknown).

**Proposed changes.** (1) Real FILES() cardinalities (C1) so nation/region are broadcast and never the shuffled side; note this does not by itself recreate the DELIM shape, which needs (2) remote runtime filters implemented in the translator/CN, mapping `THashJoinNode.build_runtime_filters` / `TPlanNode.probe_runtime_filters` onto the engine's dynamic-filter channel (`docs/super-sirius/dynamic-filters.md:58-94`); the FE already pushes them through aggregates (`AggregationNode.pushDownRuntimeFilters :448-464`). Confidence high on the diagnosis, low on the effort of (2). A CN->FE "re-plan" request does not exist and is not a feasible interim.

#### P3 (confirmed with a corrected mechanism). The FE's BROADCAST vs SHUFFLE choice is data-blind; on 4 CNs it shuffles the large table and keeps only narrow-key broadcasts

**Measured.** With 4 CNs alive, 16 of the 27 broadcast joins in the 15 passing queries flip to PARTITIONED (plan-summary.txt vs plan-summary-4cn.txt); q20 and q22 are unchanged. The big movers on 4 CNs (card-compare-cn4.txt, cn4-cnlog.json per-stream nixl bytes, cn4-transmits.txt):

| query | shuffled / broadcast stream | actual rows | nixl GB per run | what a size-aware plan would move (measured 1-CN parked size of the small side) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| q03 | exch 2 SHUFFLE lineitem | 3,234,397,656 | 58.2 of 60.34 | broadcast orders x customer, 2.33 GB parked (cn1-ops.txt) -> ~7 GB |
| q10 | exch 8 SHUFFLE lineitem; exch 5 SHUFFLE customer | 1,480,675,200; 150,000,000 | 26.65 + 19.15 of 48.04 | broadcast filtered orders 0.70 GB and lineitem x orders 2.29 GB -> ~9 GB |
| q12 | exch 1 SHUFFLE orders | 1,500,000,000 | 23.09 of 23.47 | broadcast filtered lineitem 0.51 GB -> ~1.5 GB |
| q07 | exch 8 SHUFFLE lineitem (build vs a 799,746-row probe); exch 13 SHUFFLE orders; exch 17 BROADCAST customer | 1,822,871,264; 1,500,000,000; 600,000,000 (150M x 4) | 43.75 + 13.50 + 3.71 of 69.01 | broadcast supplier x nation (~800K rows) and nation |
| q22 | exch 10 BROADCAST orders `o_custkey` | 6,000,000,000 (1.5B x 4) | 18.56 | build on the ~6M filtered customers (RIGHT ANTI), see P5 |
| q04 | exch 5 SHUFFLE lineitem (LEFT SEMI build) | 3,793,363,900 | 22.76 of 23.64 | RIGHT SEMI with the 57M filtered orders as build |
| q19 | exch 4 SHUFFLE lineitem | 128,557,109 | 2.70 | broadcast filtered part 0.02 GB; no measurable cost today |

Drain time on the critical path at 4 CNs (finding B5): q03 0.28 s of a 1.42 s span (20%), q10 0.26-0.29 s of 1.48 (17-19%), q12 0.12 of 1.08 (11%), q19 and q14 4-6%.

**Mechanism, corrected by the source skeptic.** The cited term `CostModel.visitPhysicalDistribution` BROADCAST = `outputSize * aliveBackendNumber` (`CostModel.java:419-424`) is inert in this deployment: the Sirius CNs register as COMPUTE NODEs (`experimental/starrocks/src/lib.rs:210-212` `ALTER SYSTEM ADD COMPUTE NODE`; cn4/cluster.log:201 `run_mode is shared_data`), and `ctx.getAliveBackendNumber()` counts only BACKENDs (`system/SystemInfoService.java:1047`), so it is 0. The node count enters through `HashJoinCostModel.getMemCost` (`sql/optimizer/cost/HashJoinCostModel.java:115-127`: `beNum = max(1, aliveBackendNumber + aliveComputeNodeNumber)` in shared-data mode, `memCost = rightOutput * beNum` for BROADCAST, weight 2 in `CostModel.getRealCost`). With every child at 1 row, `Statistics.getOutputSize` is the sum of projected type widths, and the rule reduces to: broadcast the right side iff its row width is below roughly the left width at 1 CN, and below roughly a quarter of it at 4 CNs. This reproduces every observed decision (q03: build 16 B vs probe 24 B -> BROADCAST at 1 CN, PARTITIONED at 4; customer 4 B vs orders 20 B -> BROADCAST at both; the survivors q22 `o_custkey` 4 B, q07 `c_custkey+c_nationkey`, q02 `ps_partkey+min` are the narrow ones). `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` (`task/EnforceAndCostTask.java:281-325`) never fires because it needs `rightChildStats.getOutputRowCount() > 15,000,000` (`SessionVariable.java:1833`).

**What a row-count-only fix would and would not do (inference, hand computation of the FE cost code, medium confidence).** Giving FILES() scans a row count but leaving column stats UNKNOWN makes the FE estimate a join output as `max(L, R)` and range predicates at 0.5, so orders x customer in q03 is estimated at 375M-750M rows. That *arms* `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` against the broadcast the finding wants: broadcast is rejected when the right side is > 15M rows and the left is less than 10x its bytes (`EnforceAndCostTask.java:324-325`). Result: q12 and q19 flip to BROADCAST (saving ~26 GB), q03 and q10's customer join stay PARTITIONED, q14 stays a wash. Getting the q03/q10 plans additionally requires raising `broadcast_row_limit` / `broadcast_right_table_scale_factor` (`SessionVariable.java:1833-1836`), or column statistics (NDV) for FILES(), or neutralising the probe-cache penalty in `HashJoinCostModel` (`BROADCAST_MAT_RATIO` 12 vs `SHUFFLE_MAX_RATIO` 3).

**Existing levers.** SQL join hints `JOIN [BROADCAST|SHUFFLE]` are honoured (`sql/parser/AstBuilder.java:6567-6575`, `JoinHelper.java:344-349`), but the grammar accepts them only in explicit `JOIN ... ON` syntax, not the kit's comma joins, and a hint disables reorder/commutativity for that join. `broadcast_row_limit = 0` forces shuffle everywhere (`EnforceAndCostTask.java:312-314`), which would help q22/q07/q02 and hurt q03/q12/q19. `cbo_debug_alive_backend_number` (`SessionVariable.java:1823`) changes only the BE count and cannot reproduce the 1-CN plan at 4 CNs.

Confidence: high on the flip and the byte inflation; medium on the corrected cost arithmetic (not executed in the FE).

#### P4 (confirmed, impact narrowed). Every CN statement pays a fixed ~120-270 ms before the first fragment runs

**Measured** (first `fragment run started` minus `runs.csv start_utc`, agent-notes/mfs3_decomp.py, warm runs): cn1 q02 195/189 ms, q11 233/227, q15 193/190, q22 199/136; cn4 q02 175/200, q11 262/257, q15 206/211, q22 118/155. All 15 passing queries pay it: 127-239 ms (cn1), 118-270 ms (cn4). The tail after the last fragment is 2-8 ms. Standalone pays 9-22 ms, measured in-process.

Decomposition of cn1 q02.r1 (client start 13:03:24.267; cn1/cluster.log RPC spans):

| phase | window | ms |
|---|---|---:|
| mysql process + handshake (`select @@version_comment limit 1`, planned as UNION_NODE and refused by the CN) | +0 .. +13 | 13 (18-57 across runs) |
| 8 `get_file_schema` RPCs, one per FILES() CTE in the WITH clause (5 of them for tables q02 never reads); lineitem call busy 28.3 ms + idle | +20 .. +93 | 73 (median across runs 104 cn1 / 114 cn4) |
| FE planning, no CN activity | +93 .. +147 | 54 |
| deploy: 13 `exec_plan_fragment` RPCs in 6 topological levels, ~40 ms dead time after every multi-reply level | +150 .. +329 | first fragment runs at +194.6 |

Sources: `TableFunctionTable.java:264 -> getFileSchema():688-712` (one RPC per FILES() reference, no cache); `experimental/starrocks/src/file_schema.rs:62-70` reads every footer serially (60 for lineitem) and deliberately ignores the FE's `schema_sample_file_count` = 2 (`file_schema.rs:52-58`, `TableFunctionTable.java:114`). Deploy waves are the per-level loop in `AllAtOnceExecutionSchedule.schedule` over `ExecutionDAG.getFragmentsInTopologicalOrderFromRoot()` (`qe/scheduler/dag/ExecutionDAG.java:195`), root first, so the leaf scans arrive in the last levels and the whole deploy sits on the critical path.

**Corrections.** The head does not "cap the 4-CN speed-up": with it removed, engine-only speed-ups are q02 1.10x, q22 1.12x, q11 1.83x, q15 2.46x, so only q11 is materially affected. It is 28%/36%/9%/37% (q02/q11/q15/q22) of the gap to standalone, not the dominant reason. FE-side cost is ~215 ms (cn1) vs ~205 ms (cn4) for q11.r1 from the AuditLog, so it does not grow with CN count. The ~40 ms inter-level gaps appear only after levels with two or more replies on one connection and are most likely Nagle + delayed ACK on the CN's accepted sockets (no `set_nodelay` in `experimental/starrocks/src/brpc.rs`; only outgoing `prpc_client.rs:170`): inference, medium confidence, testable with `stream.set_nodelay(true)` at brpc.rs:114.

**Proposed changes.** (1) `file_schema.rs`: honour `schema_sample_file_count` or read footers concurrently and memoize by (path, len, mtime): saves 60-110 ms per query, high confidence. (2) Set TCP_NODELAY on accepted CN sockets (brpc.rs): saves ~40 ms per multi-reply level if the inference holds. (3) For 1 CN, test `SET enable_single_node_schedule = true` (`SessionVariable.java:3337`; `Deployer.deployFragmentsForSingleNode` issues one `exec_batch_plan_fragments` RPC, which the CN implements at `compute_node_service.rs:424-450`); FILES() qualifies (`FileScanNode` is not in `ScanNode.isConnectorScanNode`). Collapsing levels FE-side for 4 CNs is unsafe as written because stage-2 fragments carry an `is_cached` descriptor table (`Deployer.java:247-251`) that the CN resolves from a per-query cache (`compute_node_service.rs:954-988`). (4) Bench-kit hygiene: emit only the CTEs a query uses (saves 3-6 of the 8 RPCs; does not fix real users).

content.content:
#### P5 (not adversarially verified). Semi/anti join sides, CTE inlining, lost operator fusion, dropped dynamic filters

These were analysed by one agent each and not refuted or confirmed by skeptics. Evidence is measured unless marked.

- **Semi/anti build side (PC-4, SAJ-2, SAJ-3).** q04: `5:LEFT SEMI JOIN (BROADCAST) build=4:EXCHANGE<-lineitem` with 3,793,363,900 rows (card-compare-cn1.txt line 20); 30.82 GB of `l_orderkey` parked (cn1-quent.txt q04 `STREAMING_SINK in=30.82GB`) and 22.76 GB shuffled on 4 CNs. The engine flips it internally: cn1/engine-cn0.log q04 F00 `HASH_JOIN (id=6) type: RIGHT_SEMI`, build = orders scan, probe = lineitem stream, so 1-CN time is at parity (1850 vs 1896 ms); the cost is memory and exchange volume, not time. q22: `11:LEFT ANTI JOIN (BROADCAST) build=10:EXCHANGE<-orders` 1.5B rows to every CN; per-CN `HASH_JOIN(15)` 0.516 s on 4 CNs vs 0.588 s on 1 CN (cn4-quent.txt q22.r1, cn1 q22.r0), which is why q22 scales 1.13x. Standalone uses `RIGHT_DELIM_JOIN RIGHT_ANTI` with the customer keys as build (standalone/runs/q22.explain.txt). The FE has the commutation rule (`rule/transformation/JoinCommutativityRule.java:34-44` LEFT_SEMI<->RIGHT_SEMI, LEFT_ANTI<->RIGHT_ANTI) but at cardinality 1 it never pays. The translator refuses `RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN` (`node_translator.rs:1743-1762`: the match has no RIGHT_SEMI arm, `_ => UnsupportedPlanNode "hash join type is unsupported"`) although the Substrait consumer (`substrait/src/from_substrait.cpp:558-560`) and the engine (`src/planner/sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:245,273`) support it. Proposed: add `TJoinOp::RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN => (JoinType::RightSemi, JoinOutput::Right)` plus a `JoinOutput::Right` arm; small, high confidence on feasibility.
- **Anti join emulation (SAJ-5).** `LEFT_ANTI_JOIN => (JoinType::Left, JoinOutput::LeftAnti)` at node_translator.rs:1749 is an outer join plus `IS NULL` filter because `from_substrait.cpp:540-570` lacks LEFT_ANTI/RIGHT_ANTI. Measured cost in q22: `HASH_JOIN(15) in=6.59GB` -> `FILTER(16) in=6.93GB` -> `PROJECTION(17) in=0.22GB` (cn1-ops.txt fragment 832d7f224fc8), i.e. ~97% of the join output is produced and discarded. Proposed: add the two cases to `SubstraitToDuckDB::TransformJoinOp` and map them natively (engine has `JoinType::ANTI`/`RIGHT_ANTI`, `sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:242-246`). Medium confidence.
- **CTE inlining (PC-5, MFS-1).** q15 scans lineitem twice in two fragments (cn1-quent.txt:990-1000: `GPU_SCAN n=56 in=122.25GB` in fragments 567 and 566, walls 4.434 + 2.149 s serial; standalone one scan, 2627 vs 4685 ms); q11 runs the partsupp chain twice (16.4 GB + 13.1 GB). `CTEContext.needInline` (`sql/optimizer/CTEContext.java:157-190`) inlines unless cost*ratio says otherwise, and with 1-row stats inlining always wins (`cboCTERuseRatio = 1.15`, `SessionVariable.java:1511`). `SET cbo_cte_reuse_rate = 0` would force reuse (`isForceCTE`, CTEContext.java:206-217) but the CN refuses `MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK` by name (`compute_node_service.rs:1068`, `:1519`). This is also the plan-level cause of the q15 wrong answers (section 1).
- **q13 lost DENSE_COUNT_JOIN (SAJ-4).** FE plan: `5:HASH JOIN RIGHT OUTER -> 6:Project -> 7:AGGREGATE count(o_orderkey) group by c_custkey` (survey/explain/q13.costs.txt); the Substrait keeps the Project (cn1/dump/plan-0339.substrait: `aggregate -> project -> aggregate -> project -> join`); `detect_dense_count_join` (`src/planner/sirius_plan_aggregate.cpp`) requires the aggregate's direct child to be the join. Measured: CN `HASH_JOIN(6) 1.406 s + HASH_GROUP_BY(8) 0.261 s` in a 0.558 s fragment vs standalone `DENSE_COUNT_JOIN(4) 0.066 s` (cn1-ops.txt fragment 286810da3429; standalone-quent.txt); `grep -c "Fusing COUNT-join" cn1/engine-cn0.log` = 0. Proposed: look through a pure-column `LogicalProjection` in `detect_dense_count_join`, or elide the pure-subset PROJECT under an AGGREGATION_NODE in the translator. Medium confidence; it is ~0.4 s of q13's 0.38 s gap to standalone.
- **q20 cardinality-blind pre-aggregation and dropped runtime filters (SAJ-1).** The FE aggregates all of lineitem-1994 by `(l_partkey, l_suppkey)` before the join: exch 9 = 304,124,949 rows on 1 CN, 639,885,819 on 4 CNs (card-compare); the lineitem fragment is 3.303 s of the 3.800 s span with `MERGE_GROUP_BY(4) n=6 2.903 s` (cn1-quent.txt q20.r1); the runtime filters the FE attached to the lineitem scan (`filter_id 2/3, remote=true`, survey/explain/q20.costs.txt) are dropped. Standalone joins lineitem with the 8.69M delim keys below the aggregate (`DYNAMIC_FILTER(25)` on the scan) in 2.958 s. Proposed: implement remote runtime filters (as in P2) or, as an interim, honour the FE's STREAMING pre-aggregation mode as pass-through in `agg_phase.rs`. Medium confidence.
- **q07 dynamic filter no-op on the orders stream (FWJ-3).** cn1-ops.txt fragment 772c72f753ea: `DYNAMIC_FILTER(21)` on the 18.38 GB orders stream ran at +0.097 s, before its build published (Quent task timestamps), `PARTITION(22)` input 18.38 GB (no reduction), `HASH_JOIN(24) 0.753 s` vs standalone `HASH_JOIN(34) 0.072 s` with orders pre-filtered 18.37 -> 1.49 GB at the scan. On 4 CNs the planner logs `Not wiring dynamic filter(s): build side carries neither filter nor opaque-build evidence` (cn4/engine-.cn1.log 13:19:58.309). ~1.0 s of GPU operator time, ~0.25-0.3 s of wall in the join fragment. Proposed: treat a declared stream far below the base table as filter evidence (`src/planner/sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:646-664`) and add a dependency edge from the DF pipeline to the build's publish when the probe is a parked stream. Medium confidence.
- **The engine's in-fragment re-plan works, but only inside a fragment (PC-6).** Declared stream cardinalities equal actual parked rows for every stream (cn1-cnlog.txt `cards[]` vs card-compare), DuckDB reorders inner joins with them (q19: engine built on filtered part and probed the 128.6M-row lineitem stream, cn1-ops.txt 6493-6546; q07: build/probe of three joins flipped vs the FE), but `STATISTICS_PROPAGATION` is disabled (`src/sirius_ffi.cpp:233-240`), so a FILES() scan inside the same fragment keeps its raw estimate, and the fragment cut is fixed before any of this. Also see C2.
- **Two-phase aggregation is cheap (AGG-5).** q01/q06 merge and result fragments 3-24 ms, hops 1-7 ms, 20-40 ms total post-scan; parity 1.04/0.97. The translator's decimal lowering shifts ~0.5 s of summed GPU time into PROJECTION and is the 9.6e-4 deviation source. Low priority.

#### Disputed planning finding

**PC-3: "the 4-CN BROADCAST->PARTITIONED flip is the measured source of the 0.43-0.59 scaling efficiency": refuted on the causal claim, plan facts stand.** The data skeptic's objection: the efficiency band exists without any data movement. q01 moves 0.00 GB and reaches 0.59; q06 0.00 GB, 0.56; q15 1.27 GB, 0.58; q19 2.75 GB, 0.53; against q03 60.34 GB, 0.48 and q07 69.01 GB, 0.43 (results-ratios.md, cn4-transmits.txt). Movement therefore accounts for at most ~0.05-0.15 of efficiency on the heaviest queries and none of the ~0.4 baseline loss. The baseline loss is measured elsewhere: per-GB `GPU_SCAN` Computing rises 1.3-1.6x on 4 CNs for every query including the join-free ones (q01 0.047 -> 0.072 s/GB, q06 0.067 -> 0.096, q14 0.069 -> 0.112; cn1-quent.json vs cn4-quent.json top_ops), and ~0.2 s per query is outside the engine span on both arms (P4). Two attributions in PC-3 are also wrong: q07's dominant mover is the 1.82B-row lineitem shuffle (43.75 GB), not the 600M-row customer broadcast (3.71 GB); q02's are the four 800M-row partsupp shuffles (38.5 GB), not the 472M-row broadcast (4.25 GB). q12's orders shuffle is off the critical path (sender Computing 0.255 s overlapping the compute-bound lineitem scan). Keep the table in P3 as the plan-level fact; do not attribute the efficiency band to it.

### 3B. Cardinality

#### C1 (confirmed). Every FE estimate is 1 row; actuals reach 6.0e9

**Measured.** `card_all_one=True` for all 22 plans (survey/plan-summary.txt). Exchanges carrying >= 100M rows on 1 CN (card-compare-cn1.txt, last line): q02/exch3 800M, q02/exch28 800M, q02/exch34 118M, q02/exch36 118M, q03/exch8 146M, q04/exch4 3,793M, q05/exch1 150M, q05/exch4 228M, q07/exch8 1,823M, q07/exch12 1,500M, q07/exch16 150M, q10/exch12 115M, q13/exch2 1,484M, q13/exch4 150M, q14/exch3 200M, q19/exch3 129M, q20/exch9 304M, q20/exch12 800M, q21/exch6 731M, q22/exch10 1,500M. On 4 CNs (card-compare-cn4.txt) the list grows to 26 entries and the summed broadcast rows reach 6,000M (q22/exch10).

**Source.** `StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676` (quoted in P1). Reached for FILES() via `visitLogicalTableFunctionTableScan` (:374-375). Consequences confirmed in source: `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` inert (P3); CTE inlining always wins (P5); `JoinCommutativityRule` never commutes semi/anti (P5); the translator comment at `node_translator.rs:1918-1929` already records that "the FE reports cardinality: 1 for every FILES() external scan" and that "bounding it belongs to the executor".

**Where row counts already exist.** (a) FE-only, no wire change: `TableFunctionTable.parseFilesForLoadAndQuery` records every file's byte size (`catalog/TableFunctionTable.java:611 brokerFileStatus.setSize(fileStatus.getLen())`, exposed via `loadFileList()` :300); `computeFileScanNode` can estimate rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema. (b) Exact: `file_schema.rs:19-27` already opens every footer (`ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder` metadata) for the schema RPC; `FileMetaData.num_rows` is available but `PGetFileSchemaResult` carries only status + schema (`gensrc/proto/internal_service.proto:647-650`), so this is a proto + FE + CN change, not FE-only. (c) Later: per-column min/max from row-group stats for the date range predicates.

**Limits (inference, from the FE estimator code).** Row counts without column statistics leave `ColumnStatistic.unknown()` in place: range predicates on unknown columns cost 0.5 (`BinaryPredicateStatisticCalculator.estimatePredicateRange` -> `OVERLAP_INFINITE_RANGE_FILTER_COEFFICIENT`), IN 0.5, string equality 1.0, and join output = `max(L, R)` (`StatisticsCalculator.computeJoinNode :1219-1240`). That separates lineitem from nation and orders from region, which is what the fragment cut needs most, but it also arms the broadcast guard against mid-sized broadcasts (P3) and gives no NDV for the aggregate outputs that decide q02's join 37. Verify with `EXPLAIN COSTS` on q05/q22/q03 after the change; this was not run.

Confidence: high on the defect; medium-high on fix (a); the predicted plan outcomes are inference.

#### C2 (confirmed). The receiver-first exact cardinality mechanism is correct but arrives too late and is undermined by a flat 0.2 selectivity on the FE's `IS NOT NULL` conjunct

**Measured.** `engine.rs:551-590` sums parked `output_row_count` over local senders and remote batch rows and calls `declare_input_cardinality` before `build()`; `src/include/exec/stream_bind_catalog.hpp:42-47` feeds it to DuckDB's TableFunction cardinality callback. Every declared count equals the actual parked rows (cn1-cnlog.txt `cards[]` vs card-compare-cn1.txt). It only helps inside a fragment: q19's engine plan builds on the filtered part and probes the stream (cn1-ops.txt 6493-6546: `STREAMING_SOURCE(4)->DYNAMIC_FILTER(5)` 3.66 GB -> 0.01 GB, fragment 150 ms) although the FE made lineitem the build.

**BJ-4 (not adversarially verified, medium confidence).** In q10 the receiver builds on the 150M-row, 25.5 GB customer x nation side instead of the 114.7M-row, 2.29 GB stream (cn1-ops.txt 3437-3573: `PARTITION(8) 25.55 GB 0.479 s, CONCAT(9) 0.114 s, HASH_JOIN(14) 0.301 s`; the stream is behind `DYNAMIC_FILTER(11)`, i.e. probe). The translated plan carries `Filter[is_not_null($0)](customer Read)` from the FE's null-rejecting scan conjunct (`expr_translator.rs:630/929 is_not_null_pred`), and DuckDB applies `DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY = 0.2` to it (`duckdb/src/include/duckdb/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.hpp:57`), so 150M x 0.2 = 30M < 114.7M declared. Standalone has no such filter and estimates customer x nation at 151.5M. The 0.2 arithmetic is inferred from source, not from a printed estimate. Proposed: do not emit the FE's join-key `IS NOT NULL` conjunct as a Filter rel (the join drops nulls anyway), or attach it to the ReadRel as a table filter.

#### C3 (confirmed, one correction). The engine's own reservation estimate is exact once a pipeline has history, but the cold-start estimate is 8x, and four cold-start scan tasks reserve 58-80% of the pool

**Measured** (agent-notes/req_hist.py, raw Quent Reserving records). q01: after the first task completes, each scan task requests exactly its measured peak (6.98 GB for a 2.41 GB input, 2.9x); the first 4 tasks of every scan pipeline request 19.52 GB each (histogram `{8.1: 4, 2.9: 103}`). q06: 13.32 GB x 4 then 3.74 GB. Source: `src/op/scan/sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:66 kMaxNumericCarrierExpansion = 8`, `:648-668 no_history_peak_memory_estimate` = bytes x 8 + filter working set; `gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:872-880` takes the no-history branch for every task dispatched before the first completion. Max concurrent reservation held by the 4 slots (agent-notes/bj6_sweep.py): q03 79.6 GiB, q10 75.9, q12 79.7, q14 67.7, q19 58.0 on cn1; the same per CN on cn4 and in standalone. Reservations are charged to the same counter as live allocations (`cucascade/src/memory/reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:525-531`), and the engine's `[gpu_pool]` running peak reached 99.16 GB (92%) inside q03.r0's lineitem fragment and 106.09 GB (98.8%) in q04.r0 (cn1/engine-cn0.log windows 51 and 65).

Summed request vs summed peak (reservation-ratio.txt): cn1 q11 236.2 GB vs 4.3 GB (54x), q14 15.2x, q03 14.2x, q10 6.3x; cn4 q11 67.7x; standalone q13 549.8 GB vs 0.9 GB (611x, DENSE_COUNT_JOIN path), q14 68x. On 4 CNs every CN pays the 4-task wave per fragment, which is the whole of the higher 1.27/1.64 ratios for q01/q06.

**Correction to BJ-6.** The gate did trip at 1 CN: every Reserving > 10 ms in q10/q12/q14 ends exactly when another task releases (agent-notes/refute-bj6/slow_reserving.py: q10 r0/r1/r2 177.1/177.7/174.4 ms for a 20.4 GB request while 3 tasks held 61.1 GB plus 31.6 GB of leaked parked data, finding B4; q12 108.6 + 47.0 ms; q14 128-139 ms), reproducibly in all three runs, 0 at 4 CNs and in standalone. `memory_space::make_reservation` blocks on a notification channel until a release (`cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:257-266`, `notification_channel.cpp:47-59`). Cost <= 0.18 s per query today.

**q20 partial-aggregate growth (SAJ-6, measured).** exch 9 carries 304,124,949 rows on 1 CN and 639,885,819 on 4 CNs (2.1x) because each CN pre-aggregates a quarter of lineitem-1994 with fewer duplicates per group.

**Proposed.** In `no_history_peak_memory_estimate` use the split's decoded column-buffer estimate (already computed for the history clamp, `docs/super-sirius/scan.md:42`) as the fresh-read basis, keeping 8x as fallback; or cap the no-history wave to a fraction of the space max. Verify with the Reserving histogram (first 4 requests ~7 GB) and 0 OOM reschedules. Confidence high on the mechanism; note that the documented `pipeline.num_threads 8` tuning (`configuration.md:788-800`) would make the first wave 8 x 19.5 = 156 GB of a 107 GB pool, which is the likely mechanism behind the documented 12-thread cliff (inference).

### 3C. Backpressure

#### B1 (confirmed). Receiver-first rendezvous plus one fragment at a time turn every exchange into a full GPU materialisation

**Source (verified).** `engine.rs:278-280`: `// One request at a time until the handle (and its sender) is dropped` `while let Ok(request) = requests.recv()`; `run_fragment_inner` (engine.rs:486-720) does declare -> `build()` -> `relay_from` each parked sender -> `run()` -> park (engine.rs:697-716). `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:739-745 relay_from` throws unless the source fragment has run. `local_exchange.rs:248-283 take_ready` returns a receiver only when every expected sender is complete. The remote path is also park-then-export (`EngineRequest::ExportNext`, engine.rs:91-95). #### B4 (disputed: mechanism confirmed, causal claim refuted). Fragments of a failed query keep running and park output nobody consumes; the leak is 0-38 GB per failure but decided no pass/fail here

**Source (verified).** `compute_node_service.rs:449-476 cancel_plan_fragment` only calls `results.cancel()`; its log line reads `acknowledging cancel_plan_fragment (best-effort: no engine-side abort yet)` (:468) and the docstring says teardown "is a separate work item". `engine.rs:291-316` drops parked outputs only when `run_fragment` returns `Err`, and then wipes every slot process-wide. `ResultStore.query_failures` (result_store.rs:98) is recorded but never consulted on the sender path. A translator failure before the run (q16) drops the `LocalParked` slots without `drop_parked`.

**Measured** (engine-cn0.log `[gpu_pool] allocated` at fragment boundaries, agent-notes/refute-oom5/headroom.txt `base@start`): after q05 4.69 GB carried through q06/q07; after q08 8.83 GB into q09; after q09 31.56 GB through q10..q16 (seven queries); +6.6 GB from q16's parked partsupp scan -> 38.16 GB at q17's start; after q17 4.0 GB into q18; after q18 0; after q21 36.64 GB into q22 (q22 cold 4110 ms vs 943 warm). cluster.log shows the dead query's queued senders starting after `fragment run failed` (q05: 5773, 5777, 5776, 5775 at 13:05:24.632+, the first 0.25 ms before the FE's first cancel ack). The cn1 timings of q10-q16 and q22.r1/r2 were taken with 31.6 / 36.6 GB of the pool occupied (the reservation-gate blocks in C3 need that leak to occur).

Same pattern in q03.r0/r2 and in q10.r1 (lineitem 0.145-0.159 s, customer 0.083-0.102 s), q12.r1 (0.115-0.125 s), q19.r1 (0.055-0.078 s). The Quent staging-lease probe times the pack directly: 48-52 sender-side leases per CN of ~311 MB, pack median 4.9 ms per lease = 63.5 GB/s, non-pack (lease RPC + write + transmit RPC) 0.7 ms, so pack = 84-88% of the drain for q03 (74-82% q10/q12, 18-32% q19 with 7 MB batches). Receiver-side unpack of the same frames: 0.14 ms per 303 MB (2.1 TB/s), ~30x faster than the pack.

**Source (verified).** `compute_node_service.rs:1207-1219` comment: "one FIFO request channel into ONE transport thread ... the drains still run one at a time, in the FE's destination order"; `:380-392 dispatch_worker` is one thread; `:864-872 run_ready_fragment ... .and_then(FragmentOutcome::join_into_ready)` joins the drains before yielding; `nixl_transport.rs:713-775` drain loop (`export_packed_next` per batch, lease RPC, `write_and_wait`, transmit RPC); `engine.rs:813 export_packed_next = engine_call` served by the single engine thread (engine.rs:321-324); `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:~800 kPackChunkBytes = 8 MiB` with `cudf::chunked_pack` on the default stream (~37 `next()` launches per 311 MB batch). **Corrections to the proposals.** More transport threads (b) or a non-joining dispatch worker (c) cannot deliver the claimed saving on their own: packs and fragment `Run`s share the one engine thread, so packs still serialise, and a fragment started during a drain competes with `ExportNext` in the same FIFO; the upper bound of (b)+(c) alone is the ~16% non-pack part (~45 ms per CN on q03). Packing during execution into staging leases (a, first variant) would need ~30 GB of arena per CN for q03 (15.3 GB sender-side + 14.5 GB receiver-side held 0.44-0.68 s) against 17.18 GB configured, and exhaustion is a hard failure (B6). #### Tooling defects found on the way (AGG-6, high confidence)

`scratchpad/perf/sf1000/quent_bp.py:98-104` attributes staging leases by a +-0.5 s time window, so the last run of each query inherits the next cold run's first leases (cn4 q06.r2 shows 55 leases / 25.6 GB although q06 moves 64 bytes per stream; cn4-quent.txt per-fragment lease counts are likewise attributed by time, e.g. q07.r1's 1-task nation fragment shows 184 leases). Evidence root: scratchpad/perf/sf1000 (SP). Source: /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf (WT).
Scripts written here: agent-notes/agg_tasks.py (per-task GPU_SCAN durations, Queued, reservation, Computing concurrency),
agent-notes/scan_reads.py (scan_split_read Statistics joined to runs; one task FSM; lease timing), agent-notes/req_hist.py
(reservation multiplier histogram; materialize time vs files-per-split).

## 1. Timings (results.md, results-ratios.md)

| q | standalone warm | 1 CN warm | 4 CN warm | T_cn1/T_alone | T_1/T_4 | eff |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| q01 | 4882 | 5073 | 2160 | 1.04 | 2.35 | 0.59 |

## 2. Plans (survey/explain/q01.costs.txt, q06.costs.txt, standalone/runs/*.explain.txt)

- q01 FE: 3 fragments: F00 scan+Project+AGGREGATE(update serialize, STREAMING) -> exch 3 SHUFFLE(l_returnflag,l_linestatus) ->
  F01 AGGREGATE(merge finalize)+SORT -> exch 6 GATHER (MERGING) -> F02 result. Cardinality 1 everywhere. No joins, so the
  cardinality-1 defect has no planning consequence here. card-compare: exch3 actual 4 (1 CN) / 16 (4 CN), exch6 4.
- q06 FE: 2 fragments: F00 scan+Project+AGGREGATE(update serialize) -> exch 3 GATHER -> F01 merge finalize. exch3 actual 1 / 4 rows.
- Standalone DuckDB plans are structurally identical (READ_PARQUET with pushed filters -> PROJECTION -> HASH_GROUP_BY/UNGROUPED_AGGREGATE).
- Translator output for q01 scan fragment (cn1/dump/fragment-000x "=== Plan"): 6 nested Project rels with decimal->fp64 casts and a
  `1 - l_discount` computed in fp64 then cast to decimal<16,2> and back to fp64 (the truncation source), Filter(lte l_shipdate) over Read.
- With 4 CNs the FE plans are unchanged for q01/q06 (plan-summary-4cn.txt lines 1, 11).

## 3. Where the time goes (Quent, cluster.log, FE audit)

Per-statement FE-side timeline, from the audit Timestamp (statement received) and the CN log RPC spans
(agent-notes: computed by the inline script in this session; cluster.log get_file_schema/exec_plan_fragment/fragment run lines):

| arm run | audit Time | 8 get_file_schema RPCs | first exec_plan_fragment | first fragment start | last fragment finish | tail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cn1 q01.r1 | 5171 | +6 .. +128 ms | +151 | +192 | +5168 | 3 |
| cn1 q01.r2 | 4933 | +7 .. +132 | +154 | +196 | +4930 | 3 |
| cn1 q06.r1 | 1888 | +6 .. +131 | +147 | +166 | +1886 | 2 |
| cn4 q01.r1 | 1999 | +9 .. +142 | +171 | +188 | +1996 | 3 |
| cn4 q06.r1 |  836 | +5 .. +127 | +137 | +141 | +835 | 1 |

The lineitem get_file_schema RPC alone is 91-95 ms (cluster.log 13:03:12.521 "busy=28.7ms idle=62.1ms"; 4 CN 13:19:33.767
"busy=30.9ms idle=64.6ms"): file_schema.rs::parquet_files_schema awaits parquet_file_schema(path) for each of the 60 files
sequentially (file_schema.rs:68). 8 RPCs per statement = one per FILES() CTE in the bench SQL (7 of them unused by q01/q06).
So ~130 ms of a fixed ~140-190 ms pre-scan latency is schema inference; standalone pays 13 ms total (4858 wall vs 4.845 s Quent span).
Share of wall: q01 1 CN 3.7%, q01 4 CN 9.4%, q06 1 CN 8.7%, q06 4 CN 17%.

Scan fragment (Quent task FSM; cn1-quent.txt lines 17-32, 381-391; cn4-quent.txt 39-76, 1176-1201; standalone-quent.txt 7-12, 79-84):

| arm | run | scan tasks | GPU_SCAN sum | HASH_GROUP_BY/UNGROUPED | PROJECTION | Comp sum | Queued sum | wall | busy=4 slots |

Scaling decomposition (ideal = 1-CN scan fragment / 4):
- q01.r1 4 CN 2022 ms = 188 FE front + 1768 slowest scan fragment (ideal 1239, excess 529 = 26% of wall) + 66 post-scan/tail.

## 5. Reservation estimate vs peak (req_hist.py; raw Reserving/Computing records)

- After execution history, each q01 scan task requests exactly the measured peak: 6.98 GB for a 2.41 GB input (2.9x);

header (receiver-first rendezvous); gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:135-262 (reservation, clamp, downgrade predicate), :340-400
(OOM reschedule MAX_RETRIES=100); sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:640-673; file_schema.rs:1-80; TableFunctionTable.java:688-730

775-806 (GB300 host-pinned tuning: pipeline.num_threads 8 => q1 -16%, cliff at 12).

## 8. FE scan-range granularity (cn1/dump/fragment-0004.txt, a q01 scan fragment)

per_node_scan_ranges carries 60 paths / 91 TBrokerRangeDesc byte ranges (0.74-2.58 GB each, i.e. files are cut into byte ranges,
not handed out whole). With 4 CNs the FE spreads these ranges across CNs (scan_paths.rs:70 add_ranges), which is why the CN-side
coalescer forms 27 splits per CN spanning 1-8 files (scan_reads.py files/split histogram) versus 1-2 files per split on 1 CN.
No correlation of stall time with files-per-split was found (section 4).

## 9. Findings ranked (see structured output)

1. 4-CN scan-phase scaling loss (26-31% of wall) from per-split slowdowns/stalls on O_DIRECT GPFS reads; cause of q01 stalls open.
2. 4 pipeline slots bound the scan fragment at 1 CN (busy 4/4 for 98%+, memory gate idle); CN launcher cannot raise them.
3. 8x no-history scan reservation (first 4 tasks per fragment per CN) vs 2.5-2.9x measured; blocks more slots, inflates first wave.
4. Fixed ~140-190 ms FE front per statement, ~130 ms of it FILES() schema inference (8 RPCs, lineitem 60 footers sequential).
5. Two-phase aggregation and fragment hops are cheap (20-40 ms); parity 1.04/0.97; decimal lowering shifts cost, causes 9.6e-4.
6. quent_bp.py: lease time-window misattribution and scan_split_read key mismatch.

## 4. Why nothing is freed (0 bytes) although HOST=160 GiB is configured

Every OOM cycle logs (engine log, 2503 times for q05):
- `[downgrade] [GPU:N] downgrade request not satisfied and disk memory space is not configured; data cannot be spilled`
- `after downgrade (0 bytes freed), reservation still partial (3318948864/5803790251 bytes) ... proceeding with partial reservation`

Mechanism: downgrade_executor.cpp TIER 1 iterates `_data_repo_registry.get_all()` (lines 222-227), TIER 2 the pipeline task
queue (293-300). The sender's output repositories are standalone `shared_data_repository`s that "escape
data_repository_manager_ cleanup so sender output outlives this fragment" (streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112) and the sender's
engine query has already ended (`data_repository_registry_.erase(query_id)` sirius_context.cpp:436). So parked batches
are invisible to the downgrade sweep; the warning text (357-361) blames the missing DISK tier although HOST targets exist
(165-190). sirius_ffi.cpp:1062-1066 `output_row_count` throws on a non-GPU-resident parked batch, so spilling parked
outputs also needs the relay/count path to accept HOST-tier batches.
